### Problem

A release of the engine takes 1.5 to 3 hours of the release lane, and any failure starts it over:

1. A re-run of a failed lane (`gh run rerun --failed`) replays nothing it can use: it merges the first attempt's artifacts, so a scenario that failed once keeps the lane from releasing, and the only way out is a fresh dispatch that plays every scenario again, including those that already passed on the same candidate. On 2026-11-20 and 21 this cost several full lanes.
2. After a lane, the test repository's callers stay at `@v7-next` (DiluxOne/diluxone-test, `.github/workflows/*.yml`, every `uses: DiluxOne/.github/...@v7-next`) instead of going back, so between lanes the test repository runs whatever `v7-next` last pointed at, not the released engine.

### Scope

- A lane on a candidate already tried replays only the scenarios that did not pass on that same candidate (the same commit and the same `v7-next`), takes the others' passes from the earlier run, and releases when all have passed; a new candidate replays everything.
- A re-run of the failed jobs of a lane can release once its replayed scenarios pass.
- At the end of a lane, released or not, the test repository's callers go back to the ref the lane found them at, through the same pull requests the lane already opens there.
- Tests for each, and the workflow's header comment and docs/versioning.md in step.

### Out of scope

- What the scenarios check, and the rule that `v7` moves only after every scenario passed on the candidate.
- The App's rate limit and stale release pull requests (#925).

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given a lane on candidate X where every scenario but one passed, when the lane runs again on the same X, then it plays only that scenario and releases X when it passes.
- C2: Given a lane whose only failure was one scenario, when its failed jobs are re-run and that scenario passes, then the lane releases.
- C3: Given a lane that ends, when it ends, then every caller of the test repository calls the engine at the ref it had before the lane.

### Criticality

Critical
